title: Korea Box Office: ‘The Assassin(s)’ and ‘Tazza 4’ Dominate Chuseok Holiday Weekend Surge
description: Director Hur Jin-ho‘s political crime thriller “The Assassin(s)” powered to the top of the South Korean box office over the weekend of Sep. 25–27, l
body:
Director Hur Jin-ho‘s political crime thriller “The Assassin(s)” powered to the top of the South Korean box office over the weekend of Sep. 25–27, leading a major holiday box office surge across the peak Chuseok festival frame. 

	According to data from KOBIS, the tracking service operated by the Korean Film Council, the newly opened local title generated $8 million from 1,119,156 admissions over the three-day frame across 1,532 screens, claiming 40.9% of the weekend market. the period investigation drama reconstructs the August 15, 1974 assassination attempt on President Park Chung-hee during a National Liberation Day ceremony that resulted in the death of First Lady Yuk Young-soo. The plot follows a detective, played by Yu Hae-jin, alongside a veteran newspaper society desk chief, portrayed by Park Hae-il, and a rookie reporter, played by Lee Min-ho, as they investigate missing ballistic evidence that contradicts the state’s lone-gunman verdict. Since launching on Sep. 23, the release has accumulated $11.2 million from 1,566,222 admissions.
	

	Crime saga “Tazza: The Song of Beelzebub” opened in second place, taking in $4.1 million from 566,526 admissions across 1,045 screens, accounting for 21.3% of the market. Directed by Choi Kook-hee and starring Byun Yo-han, Noh Jae-won, and Ayaka Miyoshi, the fourth installment in the comic-adapted gambling franchise follows a betrayed former online casino operator who enters the international poker circuit for a high-stakes duel of vengeance. Counting previews and holiday crowds since its Sep. 23 release, the title has earned $6.1 million from 833,030 admissions.
	

	“The Odyssey” took third place in its eighth weekend, adding $3.2 million from 364,763 admissions across 843 screens. The film took 16.6% of the weekend market. Its haul has reached $96.3 million from 11,783,301 total admissions since its Aug. 5 launch.

	Last week’s chart-topper in admissions, “The Intern,” moved to fourth place in its sophomore frame. Directed by Kim Do-young and starring Choi Min-sik and Han So-hee, the Warner Bros. Korea comedy remake generated $1.5 million from 206,347 admissions across 722 screens, capturing 7.6% of receipts. That lifted its cumulative total to $5.3 million from 756,057 viewers.

	Auteur Lee Chang-dong’s social drama “Possible Love” debuted in fifth place, earning $557,981 from 72,022 admissions across 195 screens. The Venice Grand Jury Prize winner stars Jeon Do-yeon, Sul Kyung-gu, Cho Yeo-jeong, and Zo In-sung, centering on the psychological tension between a working-class couple in the aftermath of a strike and a wealthy couple filming a documentary about them. Since its Sep. 23 bow, South Korea’s Oscar submission has amassed $890,241 from 115,938 admissions.

	“Obsession” was in sixth place in its fourth frame, grossing $542,493 from 67,619 admissions across 471 screens. The film now has $6.6 million from 849,155 ticket buyers.

	“Avengers: Endgame Encore” opened in seventh place, taking $550,939 from 63,273 admissions over the frame across 178 screens and has $941,892 from 107,950 viewers.

	“Resident Evil” was in eighth place, collecting $291,213 from 36,459 admissions. The survival horror reboot has reached $1.4 million from 186,950 total admissions.

	“Spider-Man: Brand New Day” placed ninth, pulling in $154,701 from 22,278 admissions, lifting its haul to $67.4 million from 9,032,429 admissions.

	Rounding out the top 10 was the British animated adventure “Octonauts: Above and Beyond – Season 2”, which opened with $89,565 from 12,636 admissions across 239 screens, reaching $125,089 from 17,779 viewers since its Sep. 23 debut.

	The overall market collective gross for the weekend was $19.6 million, a healthy uptick from last week’s $7.6 million, thanks to the holiday.

schema.headline: Korea Box Office: ‘The Assassin(s)’ and ‘Tazza 4’ Dominate Chuseok Holiday Weekend Surge

title: Taylor Swift Premieres ‘Patient Zero’ Music Video at VMAs, Turning Her New ‘Showgirl: Encore’ Single Into a Dramatic Ghost Story
description: It’s a love story? Hardly — it’s a ghost story. Taylor Swift brought her “Patient Zero” music video to the MTV Video Music Awards Sunday night for i
body:
It’s a love story? Hardly — it’s a ghost story. Taylor Swift brought her “Patient Zero” music video to the MTV Video Music Awards Sunday night for its official world premiere, following up the release of the single at the beginning of the weekend with visuals that take the triangle in the song into more dramatic and even spookier realms than might have been anticipated. Dakota Johnson and Colin Ferrell amping up the tension, which ultimately has reverberations that go beyond just a bad breakup.
	

	Fans had only seen a 13-second teaser for the video prior to its premiere on the CBS/MTV/Paramount+ telecast, and they now know which character the headstone was for in the cemetery Swift and Johnson visit. 


	The video is, of course, Swift’s latest directorial effort, and the occasion of her attendance at the VMAs was receiving the inaugural Artist-Director Honor. It was not her only trip to the podium; after the initial speech and video premiere, Swift came back later in the show to accept a video of the year award for “The Fate of Ophelia,” at which point she thanked Dolly Parton for her inspiration.

	The singer’s initial remarks prior to sharing the video were brief, after an introduction by Johnson. “First of all, I want to say thank you to MTV for giving this platform to music videos so long ago,” Swift began. “I got to start making music videos and being a part of music videos 20 years ago, and since then, I’ve gotten to be a part of making 60 music videos — roughly 60. Eighteen of those, I wrote and directed, and I really love writing and directing music videos. I’ve gotta tell you, though, that the main reason why I love writing and directing music videos so much is because you, the fans, make it so much fun. It’s so rewarding because you actually care about what we’re making. So, you know, I wanna say thank you to everyone who ever worked on a music video that I got to be a part of. I learned something from every single person that ever worked alongside me on these projects. Mainly I want to say thank you to the fans…
	

	“And rather than say anything else, I think rather than than keep talking, I would love to, if it’s OK with you, show you my latest music video, stsarring my friend Dakota Johnson and Colin Ferrell. Cinematography by Chivo.” 

	“Chivo” is a nickname for Oscar-winning cinematographer Emmanuel Lubezki, who often works with Steven Spielberg, and who was shooting a Swift video for the first time. She seems especially enamored of that collaboration; Lubezki’s name came up as the first and only onscreen credit at the end of the premiere.

	The video has Johnson and Farrell portraying a couple whose relationship appears on the rocks, with Swift acting as a counselor to the woman, singing lyrics about how she is the man’s ex and can tell her exactly how things will go. Things are just a little less sinister in the song’s lyrics than in the way things play out on screen. Johnson is seen getting angry with Johnson after a banquet at which he speaks, as the music drops out for a driving scene in which he seems to be gaslighting her with accusations about her drinking, after she has become upset at the sight of him flirting with female guests.



	

					‘Patient Zero’ music video
	



	The video cuts to flashback of similar experiences in which Swift, his then-companion, reacted more angrily to his infractions. There’s a headline that reads “Heiress dies of mystery illness — husband inherits billions” (with the additional explanation, “Spouse inherits estate amid unanswered questions”). Then we see the two women standing at a gravestone with a photo that suggests it was Swift’s character who was born in 1986 and died in 2022. Johnson places black roses on the headstone of Swift’s dead heiress character, with it left unclear whether she’s taken any lessons from Swift’s purely spectral counsel or not.

The Patient Zero video is finally out in the world! Getting to work with Emmanuel Lubezki was something out of a dream sequence, and I learned so much from getting to watch his genius in action. I want to thank Dakota and Colin for trusting me with their time, taste, and talent… pic.twitter.com/vkLCO167Ea— Taylor Swift (@taylorswift13) September 28, 2026


	Swift was more expansive in her remarks about the new video in a message she posted on social media immediately after the premiere. “The ‘Patient Zero’ video is finally out in the world!” she wrote. “Getting to work with Emmanuel Lubezki was something out of a dream sequence, and I learned so much from getting to watch his genius in action. I want to thank Dakota and Colin for trusting me with their time, taste, and talent (giggling with your friend because you’re twinning for an entire shoot was a new and truly delightful experience). And Colin’s turn as a villain is even more impressive when you get to be around him. He’s an absolute light and as kind as they come. Cara, thank you for agreeing to play the lusty other woman. That’s what friends are for? With the ‘Patient Zero’ video, I got to explore the cinematic and literary genres I love so much. I wanted to incorporate elements of gothic ghost stories, true crime, psychological thrillers all in a setting I hadn’t really shot in much. The house was a metaphor for the coldness of a relationship that’s faded and atrophied. Thank you to Ethan Tobman for your insightful production design, and bringing that feeling to life. My editor Chancler Haynes has outdone himself. And lastly, thank you to the VMAs for giving us a World Premiere at the place where celebrating music videos became a thing. And so much love for you guys, always.” 
	



	

					Taylor Swift at the 2026 MTV Video Music Awards held at Peacock Theater on September 27, 2026 in Los Angeles, California.
									JC Olivera
	



	Following the VMAs premiere, an alert told fans they could view “Patient Zero” on Spotify Premium, Apple Music or Amazon Music. Notably, Swift has withheld her recent videos from YouTube’s free tier for a couple of days upon release before putting them up there as well, presumably because views on non-paid services do not count toward the consumption totals that fuel the Billboard charts. It will be available on YouTube as of Tuesday, the alert noted.

	In advance of the music video’s release, Swift took to her Instagram Stories on Sunday to post a short clip of herself talking to the camera, with a dateline revealing for the first time that the “Patient Zero” video was shot all the way back in March. (Needless to say, no NDA gets respected like a Taylor Swift NDA.) It gives confirmation that she hatched the idea for a VMAs premiere half a year ago, and held onto it as a secret till this date.

	Says Swift in the IG clip: “Walking through here and seeing the way that Chivo has lit this and the way the sets are and how brilliantly Ethan has done this set design, I’m kind of rethinking the release of the video. Like, I need to figure a way to get this on TV or something. I’m sort of like: ‘Google, when are the VMAs?'” A caption under the video states the obvious: “Turns out the VMAs are Sept. 27, aka today.”

	In that quote, “Chivo” is a nickname for Oscar-winning cinematographer Emmanuel Lubezki, and “Ethan” refers to Ethan Tobman, her longtime production designer.

	Beyond her nominations at the VMAs for “The Life of a Showgirl” and “The Fate of Ophelia,” Swift was given a guaranteed trip to the podium for whatever speech or unveiling she might have in mind when CBS announced that she would be receiving the inaugural Artist Director Honor. The award is given to an artist who is accomplished behind the camera as well as in front of it. Producers have described it as analogous in stature to the VMAs’ traditional Video Vanguard award, while noting that it is an unknown whether any other artists will receive this new honor in the future.

	When she came back to accept her award for video of the year for “Ophelia,” she said, “Thank you so much for giving this award to this video… I just I loved making this video because I wanted it to seem like one continuous shot, so I learned a lot about hiding cuts in places. And I want to thank everybody who helped me on this video shoot because, just the choreography… I love so much Mandy Moore as my choreographer… production designed by Ethan Tobin, my editor Chancellor Haynes, and my cinematographer on this video I’ve gotten to work with before, he’s one of the people who gave me the confidence to actually direct videos on my own. His name is Rodrigo Prieto.
	

	“And lastly, but most importantly, I want to thank and dedicate this award to one person, without whom this wouldn’t be happening, and that person is the ultimate showgirl, Dolly Parton. Every single song that she wrote, her storytelling was so vivid and so rich… Listening to her songs, it’s like watching the best music video you have ever seen in your life every single time you hear what she has written. And man, she handled this thing with such grace and joy and love and gratitude for the fact that she got to do this, and everything that happened in her life or her career, she channeled back into love and gratitude and appreciation for her fans. I’m lucky I got to be one of them and I will always be one of them. I love you all so very much and I think that we were all very lucky to share this planet with Dolly Parton for a time, and thank you for this amazing moment.”



	

					LOS ANGELES, CALIFORNIA – SEPTEMBER 27: Taylor Swift attends the 2026 MTV Video Music Awards at Peacock Theater on September 27, 2026 in Los Angeles, California.  (Photo by John Shearer/WireImage)
									WireImage
	



	The VMAs now have CBS as their primary home, allowing Swift a much higher profile for her music video than it would have gotten prior to last year, when MTV was still seen as the show’s go-to network (although the ceremony is still simulcast on the former music network). 

	The song “Patient Zero” came out Friday morning, as a single and also as part of a quartet of previously unreleased tracks newly tagged on to her 2025 “The Life of a Showgirl” album for an expanded edition titled “The Life of a Showgirl: The Encore.” The other three new songs are “Cleveland!” (about Travis Kelce and his hometown), “Pink Clouding” and “Babylon.”

	In her announcement for the expanded edition of the album, Swift wrote that about a year ago she “took a trip to Sweden to celebrate with Max (Martin) and Shellback, my two collaborators on this album. Really we just wanted to reflect and take in how grateful we were for the moment we were in, but there was a studio there and we did what we do when we feel anything at all: We wrote more songs.”

	Of the single itself, she said in an audio clip released to radio stations, “I was hanging out with a bunch of friends, and one of my friends told us that she had been reached out to by the new girlfriend of an ex of hers, asking for guidance on if she had had the same experiences with this guy that this new girlfriend was having. And everyone in our group just immediately started saying like, ‘Oh, I’ve been through that too’, and telling the stories of when this kind of reach out had happened for them. And I thought to myself, if this has happened to all of us, it’s such an interesting kind of angle on humanity and on relationships, and I wonder if I could write something from the perspective of getting this phone call, and really only from the perspective and the side of the phone call of the ex who’s been through it before.”
	

	The theme of the song is summed up in the concluding lines: “So if you wanna kick it, then I’m with it, I’ve been there / Felt the reeling, done the healing, said the curses and the prayers / When the fever turns a dreamer into a pathetic ghost / If he’s killing you, I see you, I was patient zero.”

schema.headline: Taylor Swift Premieres ‘Patient Zero’ Music Video at VMAs, Turning Her New ‘Showgirl: Encore’ Single Into a Dramatic Ghost Story

title: Kacey Musgraves Pays Heartfelt Tribute to Dolly Parton With ‘I Will Always Love You’ Performance at MTV Video Music Awards
description: Kacey Musgraves led a touching tribute to Dolly Parton at the MTV Video Music Awards 2026, honoring the late country icon just a month after her dea
body:
Kacey Musgraves led a touching tribute to Dolly Parton at the MTV Video Music Awards 2026, honoring the late country icon just a month after her death with a rendition of “I Will Always Love You.”

	The pre-taped performance began with footage of Parton introducing the classic 1974 tune. “I’d like to leave you fellas with a little bit of advice,” she said. “Don’t criticize your wife’s judgment. You just remember who she married. Just kidding you. There’s a lot of truth in that and I would also like to say about life, I hope it treats you real kind and I hope that you have all that you ever dreamed of.”
	


	She then began singing the chorus of “I Will Always Love You” as Musgraves joined in, accompanied by a piano. Musgraves stood perched at the mic with her eyes closed for most of the performance, which was met by thunderous applause from the audience.


	Following Parton’s death in August, Musgraves dedicated her song “Rainbow” to Parton at her concert at Boston’s TD Garden, followed by a rendition of her 1977 classic “Here You Come Again.” Then, at her “Middle of Nowhere” tour stop at New York City’s Madison Square Garden just a few days later, she covered “9 to 5,” a song that she’d included in her shows over the years.

	“I’m not over it, and I’m never gonna be over it,” she told the MSG crowd regarding Parton’s death. “The world definitely lost a light, and it’s hard for me to talk about. And I know how much Dolly meant to everybody also in this room. I think why it feels so dark is it’s already hard to navigate these times right now, and then we lose a matriarch like that. It’s the closest thing we’ve ever had to royalty.”
	

	Musgraves had also shared the stage with Parton at the 2019 MusiCares Person of the Year event, where she kicked off a tribute to the country icon alongside Katy Perry for a duet on “Here You Come Again.” The Queen of Nashville herself then joined them in a white dress with flowing sleeves.

	Musgraves has been vocal about her appreciation for Parton in the past, telling Rolling Stone in 2021 that she appreciated her as a “style icon” and a “businesswoman.” “First and foremost she’s a songwriter,” she said. “But she wasn’t afraid to be a beautiful, sexy woman, proud of her femininity, proud of her body. It just seems like she didn’t ever need to shrink her flamboyant nature to fit among the men that she worked with.”

schema.headline: Kacey Musgraves Pays Heartfelt Tribute to Dolly Parton With ‘I Will Always Love You’ Performance at MTV Video Music Awards

title: Madonna Opens MTV Video Music Awards With Sabrina Carpenter and Charli xcx, Plus Sombr, Debi Mazar and More
description: Madonna performed for the first time in 23 years at the MTV VMAs on Sunday, opening the show by bringing out special guests Sabrina Carpenter and Ch
body:
Madonna performed for the first time in 23 years at the MTV VMAs on Sunday, opening the show by bringing out special guests Sabrina Carpenter and Charli xcx to perform their respective duets.

	After a 20-minute telecast delay due to the NFL game, the pop icon began her performance perched on the top of a piano as Carpenter played the keys. Dressed in a black waistcoat and knee-high boots, Madonna traded verses with Carpenter, who wore a glittery ensemble along with a beret. Madonna then descended the stairs and removed her coat to reveal a red-and-black corset as dancers lifted her onto a table that rolled around a choir in the audience wearing white veils.
	

	Madonna circled back to the stage, which had been transformed into the bathroom set from the “Danceteria” music video. Charli xcx emerged from one of the stalls to the tune of the freshly released “Danceteria Afterhours” remix, as did Madonna along with actresses Debi Mazar and Julia Garner. Throughout the performance, Seth Rogen, Andrew Watt and Sombr made cameos before the two-song spectacular came to an end. “Make some noise for Madonna!” said Charli.



	Madonna has been a perennial fixture at the VMAs since its inception, dating back to her iconic performance of “Like a Virgin” at the show’s 1984 debut. In the decades that followed, she performed “Express Yourself” in 1989, “Vogue” in 1990, “Ray of Light” with Lenny Kravitz in 1998 and, of course, alongside Britney Spears and Christina Aguilera during her last VMAs performance in 2003.

	She also led all other artists in nominations for the 2026 VMAs, earning 13 nods. Taylor Swift followed with 11 nominations, Sabrina Carpenter with nine and Ariana Grande with eight.
	


	Days before her appearance, VMAs producer Van Toffler spoke with Variety about bringing Madonna back to the stage. “Well, look, we can deny it as much as we want, but Madonna is the M in MTV,” he said. “I knew it the day I started there. She is the queen of MTV. She makes great videos. She’s provocative. She always pushed us, and this year’s performance will be no exception.”

	The pop titan is coming off of a momentous year on the back of her 15th album “Confessions II,” which was released in July. The record, her first in seven years, was a sequel of sorts to her seismic 2005 album “Confessions on a Dance Floor,” reuniting her with producer Stuart Price for 16 tracks that embraced contemporary dance music while nodding to her roots and backstory.

	Madonna kicked off the era with the debut of the lead single, “Bring Your Love,” during a surprise appearance during the second weekend of Carpenter’s headlining set at Coachella in April. In the months that followed, Madonna staged key activations including a rave at West Hollywood’s Abbey and a performance in partnership with Grindr at New York City’s Times Square. Following the release of “Confessions II,” she dropped new versions of several songs including “Love Sensation” featuring Kylie Minogue and “Danceteria Afterhours” with Charli xcx, which arrived just days before the VMAs performance.

schema.headline: Madonna Opens MTV Video Music Awards With Sabrina Carpenter and Charli xcx, Plus Sombr, Debi Mazar and More

title: ‘Avengers: Doomsday’ Co-Director Explains It’s ‘Very Difficult’ to Evolve Marvel Characters, but ‘We Need to Surprise Ourselves’ and ‘Audiences’
description: “Avengers: Doomsday” co-director Anthony Russo has opened up about the pressure that comes with evolving the franchise’s iconic superhero characters
body:
“Avengers: Doomsday” co-director Anthony Russo has opened up about the pressure that comes with evolving the franchise’s iconic superhero characters, explaining that finding the balance between moving the story forward and honoring those already-beloved characters can be “very difficult.”

	“It’s a very difficult part of the process because, I mean, we basically just have to use our own meters because we love the characters, we love the history, we love them in the same way that many fans do,” Russo said during a Q&A after a screening of “Avengers: Endgame Encore” (via GamesRadar+).
	

	He continued: “But the one thing we always like to remind people of, you know, fandom does not speak with a single voice. There’s a wide variety of opinion in terms of who responds to which characters and which versions of which characters people respond to, it’s a very complex relationship that people have with the characters.”


	Russo also said that he and his brother and co-director Joe have “a lot of respect for the storytelling journey that these characters have had up to this point.” “That’s part of their magic, a big part of their magic. But at the same time, we need to surprise ourselves in terms of who those characters are, where they can go, what they can do, what can happen, and in doing that, we hopefully surprise audiences as well.”

	The director’s comments come nearly a year after an “Avengers: Doomsday” trailer spotlighted a much more serious Thor (Chris Hemsworth) than Marvel fans had seen in 2022’s “Thor: Love and Thunder.” The Taika Waititi-directed film performed well at the box office upon its release, but it divided fans who felt the character had become, in Hemsworth’s own words, “too silly.”
	

	Russo also revealed that the film’s full cast has yet to be announced. “The cast is so large, and we’ve announced some of the cast, and we haven’t announced some of the cast,” said Russo. “I get confused myself over who we’ve announced and not announced, so I have to just slow down.” So far, the confirmed cast includes Hemsworth, Robert Downey Jr., Chris Evans, Paul Rudd, Simu Liu, Tom Hiddleston and more.

	“Avengers: Doomsday” will hit theaters on Dec. 18.

schema.headline: ‘Avengers: Doomsday’ Co-Director Explains It’s ‘Very Difficult’ to Evolve Marvel Characters, but ‘We Need to Surprise Ourselves’ and ‘Audiences’

title: Neil Patrick Harris to Star in ‘Damn Yankees’ Broadway Revival
description:
A revival of “Damn Yankees,” starring Neil Patrick Harris and Julianne Hough, will open next spring on Broadway.

	It’s the first Broadway revival o
body:
A revival of “Damn Yankees,” starring Neil Patrick Harris and Julianne Hough, will open next spring on Broadway.

	It’s the first Broadway revival of “Damn Yankees” in more than 30 years. Following last fall’s run at D.C.’s Arena Stage, this revised production features a book by Will Power and Dough Wright, with additional lyrics by Lynn Ahrens and direction and choreography by Sergio Trujillo. 


	“Damn Yankees,” which revolves around a middle-aged man who makes a Faustian bargain for his losing baseball team to somehow beat the unstoppable New York Yankees, debuted on Broadway in 1955 with Robert Shafer, Gwen Verdon, Ray Walston and Stephen Douglass. It won seven Tony Awards, including best musical. Richard Adler and Jerry Ross wrote the music and lyrics, with a book by George Abbott and Douglass Wallop. The show was last revived on Broadway in 1993 with Jarrod Emick, Bebe Neuwirth and Victor Garber.
	

	“’Damn Yankees’ has always been one of our great American musicals, but I wasn’t interested in simply reviving it,” says Trujillo. “This ‘revisal’ preserves the heart, wit and soaring score that audiences love and is a real opportunity to bring joy back into the theater. ‘Damn Yankees’ is a celebration of America, and I hope audiences see themselves in it and remind them of the magic that only a great American musical can deliver. Let’s play ball!”


	This revival moves the original 1950s-set story into the 21st century. Here’s the official logline: “It’s the early 2000s, and diehard baseball fan Joe Boyd dreams of seeing his beloved Baltimore Orioles return to glory. So when a charming stranger and his captivating accomplice arrive with an offer too good to refuse, Joe makes a deal that could give both him and his team a second chance. There’s just one catch…”
	

	Harris will play the devil in disguise known as Applegate, Hough is making her Broadway debut as Lola and Austin Scott is playing Young Joe. The rest of the cast has yet to be announced.

	Harris won a Tony for the 2014 revival of “Hedwig and the Angry Inch” and has hosted the Tony Awards several times. He was recently on Broadway in “Art,” a play revival in which he starred alongside James Corden and Bobby Cannavale.

	“I’ve never done the big Broadway musical, with a big ensemble and dance numbers. It’s been a bucket list for me,” Harris said during a press conference on Sunday at Yankees Stadium. Of his character, he added, “Playing someone who is devilish is always good. It’s fun to be naughty. I want Applegate to be as alluring and puppet-mastery as possible.”

	“Damn Yankees” will play at the Marquis Theatre, with previews beginning on March 24 ahead of opening night on April 20. 

	In a first for Broadway, Major League Baseball and its production label MLB Studios will serve as a partner on the production.

	“Baseball is mythology. Broadway is mythology. They both deliver thrilling, unrepeatable live entertainment to millions of fans each year,” said Haley Swindal, who serves as lead producer with Lia Vollack (“MJ”) and Julie Boardman. “Bringing them together — with MLB at the table and this extraordinary creative team — isn’t just a revival. It’s a collision of American icons.”

	Swindal is the granddaughter of legendary New York Yankees owner George Steinbrenner. Nicknamed “The Boss,” Steinbrenner was also a Broadway producer who invested in six productions, including the 1970 Tony Award-winner “Applause” and the 1974 musical “Seesaw.”

	Noah Garden, MLB’s deputy commissioner of business and media, added, “We’re thrilled to partner with the entire team on the return of ‘Damn Yankees’ to Broadway, led by such great talents in Neil, Julianne and Austin. It’s incredibly important that our game continues to resonate outside the diamond and into different areas of culture. Baseball and Broadway fans both love high drama, high stakes and high hopes that they’re about to watch something unforgettable happen. ‘Damn Yankees’ celebrates that shared spirit, and we’re proud to help bring that energy to the stage.”

schema.headline: Neil Patrick Harris to Star in ‘Damn Yankees’ Broadway Revival

title: Jeff Probst Says ‘Survivor’ Needs Diversity Despite Paramount’s DEI Rollbacks: ‘All Those Differences Matter in the Story’
description:
Fifty seasons later, one key factor of “Survivor” remains the same: the show’s approach to diversity.

	Longtime host Jeff Probst told The New York
body:
Fifty seasons later, one key factor of “Survivor” remains the same: the show’s approach to diversity.

	Longtime host Jeff Probst told The New York Times that “nothing has changed” in the reality competition series’ approach, despite Paramount’s rollback of DEI initiatives to align with Trump’s mandates in 2025.

	Diversity, he explained, is integral to the show’s functionality. “And if you watch our show, you know that we’re so diverse — and it’s not just skin color or ethnicity. It goes much deeper than that. It’s one of the biggest positive changes ever,” Probst said. “Our stories are so much more interesting now because we have people from completely different walks of life.”
	

	He continued: “I feel no pressure. No one ever says, ‘Can you count the numbers again?’ But Jesse Tannenbaum, who runs our casting team, knows: There’s no stopping, not because we’re told to do it. This is what we need. We need diversity. It’s for narrative. All those differences matter in the story when you throw people together and force them to rely on each other while conspiring against each other. The more diverse, the more interesting.”

	While the show’s DEI initiatives have stayed the same, Probst explained how casting has changed since the show began in 2000.

	“In the early seasons, the approach to casting and storytelling was different from the kind of storytelling we’re doing now,” Probst said. “You would cast for type. And friction was part of where we were at — we wanted friction in our storytelling, arguments and finger-pointing.”
	

	Probst became more than just the host when he signed on as showrunner of the 51-season show in 2010, with the goal of making the series more cinematic.

	“I always saw the game as a device. So when I was given the reins, the three things I really wanted to do were make it more cinematic; I wanted it to dive deep into Joseph Campbell’s “Hero’s Journey”; and I wanted it to be a family show. I knew that would change who we put on the show and the types of stories that we told.”

schema.headline: Jeff Probst Says ‘Survivor’ Needs Diversity Despite Paramount’s DEI Rollbacks: ‘All Those Differences Matter in the Story’

title: ‘Roseanne’ Star Michael Fishman Apologizes to Fans for the ‘Chaos’ of Roseanne Barr Feud: ‘I’m Gonna Keep Pushing Out Love’
description: Michael Fishman, who played D.J. Conner on the ABC sitcom “Roseanne,” has taken to social media after making headlines for feuding with his former c
body:
Michael Fishman, who played D.J. Conner on the ABC sitcom “Roseanne,” has taken to social media after making headlines for feuding with his former co-star Roseanne Barr earlier this month. In August, Fishman said that the show’s 2018 reboot “was rightfully canceled” after Barr posted a racist tweet, to which Barr responded that Fishman was a “brainwashed bigot” and “a fucking little worm” in an episode of the “Can’t Be Censored” podcast.
	

	He began by apologizing to fans of the show for the“chaos over the course of the past week.” “I’ve heard from a lot of you [that you] feel like your TV family is fighting,” Fishman said in the video posted on his Instagram page. “I had the privilege of growing up with so many of you or around so many of you. And the truth is, I’m gonna keep pushing out love and light because it’s the path that I’ve chosen over the years.”


	He continued: “Our show has been a comfort show for you. So I want you to know we’re not going to ruin it. I’m going to do whatever I can to uphold that legacy and make sure it stays with you.” He added that “the show meant something to me as a kid,” and “it became even more real afterward.”

	“Gentle reminder to shine,” he wrote under the video. “We find our way home and back together.”

	Fishman appeared on all nine seasons of “Roseanne,” which ran from 1988 to 1997, and the nine-episode revival season that aired in 2018. At the time, Variety reported that the show finished its first season as the number one scripted primetime television show in the 18-49 age range. Fishman also reprised his role for four seasons on the follow-up “The Conners,” which ran for seven seasons from 2018 to 2025.
	

	See Fishman’s full video here.

Hosted by Snoop Dogg, this year’s Video Musi
body:
The 2026 MTV VMAs are in full swing, and music’s biggest stars are showing up and out on the red carpet. 
Hosted by Snoop Dogg, this year’s Video Music Awards promises audiences a jam-packed program, including a performance from Madonna (her first at the show in more than two decades), a Dolly Parton tribute and, of course, the world premiere of Taylor Swift’s “Patient Zero” music video. 2026 also marks the first time the show has returned to Los Angeles since 2017. 
In addition to Madonna and Musgraves, the night’s lineup is set to include performances from LISA, RAYE, Shaboozey, Gunna, Sienna Spiro, GENER8ION and Yung Lean. For RAYE and Sienna Spiro, the performance will be their VMAs debut.  Shaboozey will perform “Cowgirl” and then join Gunna for the first broadcast performance of their collaboration “High Noon,” while LISA will debut her new single “SaWaDiKa” on television. GENER8ION and Yung Lean will premiere “STORM II” onstage. 
Kacey Musgraves will perform the tribute to Parton, making her first appearance on the VMAs stage in five years. She is nominated for best country for “Dry Spell” this year. RAYE, Sombr and Teddy Swims will perform a tribute to George Michael. 34 years since Nirvana first performed at the VMAs in 1992, the band is set to receive this year’s Video Vanguard Award. 
In addition to her video premiere, Swift will also be honored with the inaugural Artist-Director Award. 
The 2026 MTV VMAs air live Sunday, Sept. 27 at 7:30 p.m. ET/4:30 p.m. PT from the Peacock Theater in Los Angeles.  Learn how to stream the show here.

title: Cornell Fraternity Bros' Alleged Gang Rape Case Reopened by Prosecutors
description:
Alleged Cornell Gang Rape
                          D.A. Cracks Case Back Open
body:
Alleged Cornell Gang Rape
                          D.A. Cracks Case Back Open
                      
                  
                                                                        Published 
                              September 27, 2026
                            7:00 PM PDT
                                                                            
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            The Cornell frat brothers accused of drugging and gang-raping a student aren't in the clear yet ... prosecutors are reopening the case.
      
    
            Tompkins County D.A. Matthew Van Houten tells ABC News he plans to put the 2024 case before a grand jury with the alleged victim's cooperation.
      
    
            The apparent reason for the U-turn? Her explosive civil lawsuit. Van Houten says the lawsuit tells a "dramatically different" story than the one she originally gave police.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            He claims she never initially said she was unknowingly drugged, forced into sexual activity or incapacitated.
      

            Her attorney says that's not the whole story ... arguing she was never interviewed by a specially trained detective or prosecutor after reporting the alleged attack.
      
    
            Then there's the Snapchat chat ... Van Houten says prosecutors never saw the messages, but her legal team insists police had them in 2024 and simply failed to follow up.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                                  
      
    
            As TMZ previously reported, the woman claims seven Chi Phi members gave her ketamine and sexually assaulted her inside the frat house. She alleges one member invited others upstairs by messaging the fraternity's Snapchat group that there was "free p***y."
      
    
            Cornell says it investigated the allegations, but federal privacy law prevents the school from revealing any punishment. Chi Phi remains barred from campus.
      
    
            Attorneys for two of the accused men deny wrongdoing. No one was charged the first time around ... but prosecutors are now giving the case another shot.

title: AEW Star PAC Dead at 40
description:
AEW Star PAC
                          Dead at 40 ...
                          Day After Final M
body:
AEW Star PAC
                          Dead at 40 ...
                          Day After Final Match
                      
                  
                                                                        Published 
                              September 27, 2026
                            7:28 PM PDT
                                                                            
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            AEW star PAC is dead at 40 ... stunning news that comes less than a day after he wrestled and appeared throughout the company's biggest show of the weekend.
      
    
            All Elite Wrestling announced PAC's death Sunday night, remembering the British wrestler -- real name Benjamin Satterley -- for his innovative high-flying moves and incredible in-ring ability.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                                  
      
    
            PAC competed Saturday at AEW's All Out pay-per-view in Chicago, challenging Andrade El Idolo for the AEW National Championship.
      

            He lost the match and shook Andrade's hand afterward ... but that wasn't PAC's final appearance of the night.
      
    
      
      pac's final appearance in a pro wrestling ring last night at aew all out in chicago.heartbreaking. 💔 pic.twitter.com/p6qN4n1ksQ
              @theaesthetic
  
    
            PAC later returned during the main event ... getting involved in the AEW World Championship match between fellow Death Riders member Jon Moxley and Will Ospreay.
      
    
            AEW did not reveal a cause of death or any other details surrounding his passing.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                                  
      
    
            The Newcastle, England native began wrestling in 2004 and joined AEW in 2019 ... becoming the inaugural AEW All-Atlantic Champion and a two-time AEW World Trios Champion.
      
    
            Before AEW, Satterley competed in WWE as Neville ... winning the NXT Championship and becoming a two-time WWE Cruiserweight Champion.
      
    
            RIP
